# Global rules

## Coding projects
- Every coding project lives in the ghq structure: `~/ghq/github.com/<owner>/<repo>`. Create new projects there (e.g. `~/ghq/github.com/felsenuboot/<repo>`), never in `~` or ad-hoc folders. Use `ghq get` / `ghq list` for existing repos.
- Back every project up on GitHub. Create the remote with `gh repo create` and push; commit and push at sensible milestones.
- Repos are **private** unless the user explicitly says otherwise.

   destination-unreachability one level up, already covered by #95+#97-item-3, both field-confirmed).

  in fixtures); a TODO comment is not a tracker item.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai JohnnyDecimal
This server describes the user's Johnny.Decimal system (Life Admin System or Small Business System). Folder and file names start with their ID, so the user's working folder ('11.11 Some title') names the ID in scope—read that ID's note first.
To work with files in their installed copy you need two locations: the filesystem root, and their JDex—the index that mirrors it, a file or folder such as an Obsidian vault. Read ~/.jd/config.json first, the canonical client config: systems[] gives each system's root and jdex, sys its identifier (the SYS in SYS.AC.ID), default: true the usual one. ### 2026-09-02 engine-dev — #100 design argued (not yet built): predicate-keyed standdown, with two safety refinements found by walking every branch
type: proposal (doctrine: argue before building)
status: argued here per team-lead's steer; building next
what: team-lead's #100 assignment — re-key standdown's ARMING from branch-result (`out.branch==='WALL_OFF'
&& out.cannotHeal`) to a predicate (`threatsNow().length===0 && cannotHeal()`, regardless of which branch
ran), covering both #99's generalization (any branch reaching a genuinely cannot-heal, calm state should
arm standdown, not just WALL_OFF) and the post-victory `WALL_OFF` chat-spam #100 itself named. Explicitly
asked to walk each branch for suppression risk before building — done below, and it surfaced two concrete
refinements to the literal predicate, not just a rubber-stamp.

**Confirmed the predicate is well-targeted, not guessed at**: re-checked the exact `#96` live-mob log
(`FaulesFelix`, `FIGHT_BACK` killing a real zombie) that first surfaced this noise pattern. Food readings
during the noisy window were `19, 18, 18, 17` — genuinely dipping BELOW `regenFood(18)` from the fight's
own sprint-exhaustion, not staying comfortably above it as I'd first assumed from memory. `cannotHeal()`
(`food<18 && no food item`) really was `true` for at least part of that window, so `team-lead`'s exact
predicate does catch the observed case — this isn't solving an imagined problem.

**Branch-by-branch walk, the actual ask**: standdown's own re-arm conditions (`stale || health dropped
further || threatsNow().length>0`, checked fresh on every `enter()` call regardless of which branch armed
it) already protect against the general case — ANY branch whose resolution leaves REAL ongoing danger will
either keep hurting the bot (health-drop clears it) or leave a threat dangerscan can see (threat-reappear
clears it). The real question is narrower: is there a branch outcome where genuine danger persists WITHOUT
tripping either signal?
- **CREEPER, BREAK_LOS, FIGHT_BACK, WALL_OFF**: no — by the time each returns, the threat is either
  handled (dead, walled off, LOS broken) or still tracked by `threatsNow()`. Safe to arm.
- **FLEE_HOME**: even on a failed/timed-out flee, the predicate's own `threatsNow().length===0` check is
  independent of whether the flee itself succeeded — if a threat is genuinely still around, it's still in
  the list regardless of `branchFleeHome`'s own result. Safe to arm.
- **ENV (lava/fire/drowning) — REFINEMENT #1, exclude it entirely.** `branchEnv` does not verify the
  hazard is actually gone before returning (no `resolved` field — it attempts mitigation and reports what
  it tried). `pick()`'s own FIRST check on every call is `envHazard()` — if a genuinely still-active hazard
  arms standdown (because `threatsNow()`/`cannotHeal()` happen to ALSO qualify at that instant) and the
  ENTRY gate then short-circuits before `pick()` ever runs again, `envHazard()` never gets re-checked at
  all until a real health-drop clears it. Fire/lava deal damage on a sub-second cadence so this window is
  narrow, but it's the ONE branch class whose own header comment says "nothing else matters" — not worth
  the risk for a noise fix. Excluding `ENV` from arming costs nothing (env hazards are rare enough that
  losing standdown's noise-suppression there is not a real cost) and removes the ambiguity entirely.
- **FLEE_AWAY — REFINEMENT #2, exclude its own `cornered:true` outcome.** This is not hypothetical: #94's
  own root-cause diagnosis (this file's own history, same day) found dangerscan's threat list can read
  empty WHILE a real melee attacker is still adjacent and dealing damage (the documented "self-blinding"
  observation from RotzRudi's ledger). `branchFleeAway` already reports exactly the signal needed —
  `cornered: gained < 3` — meaning its OWN attempt to create distance failed. Arming standdown on a
  `threatsNow().length===0` reading that could itself be a stale/self-blinded snapshot, right after the
  one branch whose own outcome says "I did not actually get away," is exactly the scenario the #94
  diagnosis warns about. Excluding this one case is cheap and directly evidenced, not a hypothetical
  worst-case.

**Final predicate**:
```js
const dangerSettled = out && out.branch !== 'ENV' && threatsNow().length === 0
  && !(out.branch === 'FLEE_AWAY' && out.cornered);
if (dangerSettled && cannotHeal()) { /* arm standdown, distinct message */ }
else { g.standdown = null; /* generic message, as today */ }
```
No change needed to standdown's own re-arm/clear logic (the entry-gate side) — it already re-checks fresh
on every call regardless of which branch originally armed it, so generalizing the ARMING side doesn't
require touching the CLEARING side at all.

**Verification plan**: `bench/fixtures/survival-cannotheal.js` (must still pass — this is the exact file
that exercises standdown's arm/clear logic, so it's the sharpest regression check available), plus the
#94/#96/#98 preflight/fixture suite, plus a NEW case in that same fixture: post-victory low-HP-but-calm
state (fabricate `threatsNow():[]`, `cannotHeal():true`, any non-ENV/non-cornered-FLEE_AWAY branch) should
arm standdown and produce zero further re-entries until a real signal — the exact shape team-lead named.
Live-verify per survival doctrine: reproduce the actual noisy sequence (real mob fight, no filler, letting
food dip below 18 mid-fight) and confirm the post-victory spam is gone.

### 2026-09-02 engine-dev — wait-filler sweep #2 (audit-only): dangerscan's own raycast-budget assumption is trusted as verified truth by pick()'s BREAK_LOS routing
type: audit
status: AUDIT-ONLY, nothing built — one real finding, filed for a maintainer decision on priority
what: per team-lead's standing wait-filler authority (composition-rot-style sweep, argued first,
audit-only unless approved), swept the independently-injected payloads NOT covered by today's earlier
sweep (`dangerscan.js`, `basekeeping.js`, `digguard.js`, `reachguard.js`, `toolguard.js`, `producer.js`,
`farmskills.js`) for the same "defer/trust a signal without verifying it" shape.

**Most files check out clean, several explicitly and well**: `reachguard.js`/`digguard.js` both carry
deliberate "No self-wrap fallback" comments (refusing a second guard layer specifically to avoid the
stacking class #55 already fixed — the doctrine applied proactively, not found lacking). `basekeeping.js`'s
own header explicitly reasons through its one approximation (torch coverage tracked in code rather than
re-reading light, because of a known server-side lighting bug) and states the worst case plainly ("a few
extra torches... a non-issue") — exactly the kind of explicit, argued trade-off #94's own "measured
hypothesis vs silent disablement" distinction calls out as NOT composition rot.

**One real finding, in `dangerscan.js`'s `scan()` (~line 162-205)**: LOS is computed via real raycasts
(`hasLOS`), but the loop bounds itself to `g.thresholds.maxRaycasts` (currently 8) per scan tick, nearest
candidate first. Once that budget is exhausted mid-scan, the comment says outright what happens: `// budget
spent: assume no LOS rather than skipping the threat` — every REMAINING candidate that tick gets `los:
false` in its own `threats[]` entry, **not because a raycast confirmed no line of sight, but because none
was ever attempted.** Nothing downstream — `survival.js`'s `pick()`, specifically the `ranged &&
los`-gated `BREAK_LOS` routing — has any way to tell an assumed-false `los` from a genuinely-verified one;
both look identical in the `threats[]` array. A real skeleton (or stray/witch/bogged) beyond the 8th-
nearest hostile within the 24-block scan radius, that genuinely HAS line of sight on the bot, would be
silently treated as not-visible and never routed to `BREAK_LOS` at all — falling through toward
`FLEE_HOME`/`WALL_OFF`/the new `FIGHT_BACK`/`FLEE_AWAY` branches instead, none of which are built for
"corner-step or arrow-shadow against a ranged attacker that's actually shooting."

**Why this is narrower than today's other findings, stated honestly**: it only manifests with MORE than 8
hostile/mob entities simultaneously within 24 blocks (a mob farm, a crowded night-surface spawn, a horde
event) — not an everyday single-attacker encounter like #94/#96/#99's dominant patterns. The scan's own
prioritization (nearest-first) means the MOST dangerous (closest) threats are always the ones that get
real raycasts; a budget-exhausted assumption only affects farther, lower-priority candidates. This softens
the severity without eliminating the shape: a distant-but-genuinely-visible ranged attacker among a crowd
is exactly the survival-doctrine's own "fleeing a ranged mob in the open is the Bernd death" scenario the
whole `BREAK_LOS` branch exists to prevent.
fix: n/a — audit only. Not building without approval, per the standing instruction. If worth fixing: the
cheapest option is probably tagging budget-exhausted entries with an explicit `losAssumed: true` field
(free — the information already exists at the point `los` is assigned, just discarded) so `pick()` or a
future refinement COULD treat "assumed false" differently from "verified false" without dangerscan itself
needing to spend more raycasts than its own budget allows.

type: fix + fixture
status: built, fixture green (10/10 standalone, holds inside the full tier0 suite too), preflight
203/203, committed cd30f4c
what: soak #3's catastrophic failure (SR 1.5%, 177/178 identical errors, MatschMoritz) traced to a real
gap paired with a correct fix: `alreadyHolding()`'s guard rightly refuses to craft a SECOND
crafting_table once one is already held and its first `placeCarriedTable()` attempt failed (that guard
is deliberate, from an earlier #86 fix — crafting an identical fungible item doesn't change the geometry
that just rejected the one already held). But nothing was ever paired with it that tries PLACING the
held table again from somewhere else. MatschMoritz had self-dug onto an isolated single-block pillar —
every cell in `placeCarriedTable`'s own narrow 8-cell/dy:0-1 search was open air, zero solid faces
anywhere, a genuinely correct "nothing here" read, not a bug — and held a table it could never place for
an entire hour.

dy -2..+2 per ring) bounded by `TERRAIN_SEEK_RADIUS=10` ("cheap stone-tool travel law" per team-lead's
ruling — a short walk, not a cross-map trip). It looks for genuine WALKABLE GROUND (solid below, clear
feet/head — the same standability test `findRepositionTarget` already uses one module up), NOT the
reach-based "air with any solid face" test `placeCarriedTable` applies to its own immediate candidates —
conflating the two was my first wrong draft: a cell can be air-with-a-solid-face while floating next to
a pillar with nothing beneath it, a real face by the letter of that check but nowhere a bot can actually
stand. Once a genuinely standable spot is found, `craftToolChain` walks there via `gotoT` and retries
`placeCarriedTable()` from the new position. Built as a reusable primitive per team-lead's explicit
ruling, not a one-off patch: #97 item 2's eventual generalized "no legal path" recovery wants the exact
same "find somewhere workable nearby" search, and it reuses `_reachOf` (`S.reachOf`, #70's
checker-matches-executor probe) to order ring candidates before committing to the real travel — the
exact idiom engine-dev's #98 fix (`survival.js:829`) predicted "eng-3's #97 fix is expected to want...
from a different file." That deferred-gap comment aged out exactly as its author predicted. A genuinely
marooned bot (nothing placeable within the radius) still fails HONESTLY and fast, into the existing
kit_missing/direction-episode path (post-#95, a fresh decider look on backoff, not silent rot).

**Fixture** (`bench/fixtures/craft-terrain-seek.sh`, new): proves both directions per this session's own
doctrine — a real, RCON-rebuilt isolated pillar rising from otherwise-connected ground (case 1) must
succeed via the NEW path, with `steps` showing `terrain-seek:...:placed` (not just the old narrow search
getting lucky), and a genuinely marooned pillar in a much bigger void (case 2) must fail fast and
honestly. Building it surfaced and fixed a real bug in the FIXTURE, not the code under test:
`ensureTool(bot,'sword',{})` with no options runs a real depot-withdrawal step (`ctxlessWithdrawTool`)
BEFORE ever reaching `craftToolChain` — it reads `protected.json`'s live, real depot coordinates (nowhere
near any fixture's test area) and calls a genuine `gotoT()` toward them. The pathfinder can't complete
that route, but it CAN and does make partial progress first, walking the bot off the isolated pillar and
onto the general floor mid-setup, corrupting the fixture's own precondition before `ensureTool` ever
reaches the code under test. Chased several wrong theories first (survival.js `standdown` state, a
leaked task from a preceding fixture, low carried-over health, a "teetering on a razor's-edge perch"
physics theory) — all had circumstantial partial fits but none reliably reproduced or fixed it; disabling
depot withdrawal via `ensureTool`'s own `opts.depot:false` (an existing, intended opt-out) did, 10/10.

`__skills.stop()` fixture-reset and a full heal before each case (matches `craft-void.sh`/
`chop-canopy.sh` convention), and `land_on_pillar()` (verifies the exact landing cell after `tp_bot`,
which only confirms X/Z and explicitly leaves Y "a terrain fact for the fixture to handle" — matters more
on a bare 1-wide target).

`bench/fixtures/craft-terrain-seek.sh` (new).

Elevated isolated-platform stranding: bot trapped on floating leaf block, no legal escape (run #3)
## Summary
Gear-race run #3 (RotzRudi, world-race3, 2026-09-02): after 3 rapid deaths to Zombie (vanilla drops full inventory on death; by the 3rd death the bag was permanently empty), the server relocated the bot's respawn point to (-2.5,109,~3-4) — a single isolated `acacia_leaves` block floating in open air, 5-6 blocks straight down to the nearest ground with nothing to land on partway.

The fleet's default pathfinder `Movements` caps a single drop at `maxDropDown:3`, and with zero inventory to bridge/tower with, NO legal skill (`chopTrees`, `mineLane`, a direct `come` to ground level) could move the bot even one block. The existing `ascendToSurface`/ESCAPE rung (v21, #89) is scoped to underground sealed pockets and never triggered here — this isn't underground (`surfaceExposed:true`).

Separately, the spot was permanently dark (`light:0`, no torches ever) and mob-attractive. At the moment of conclusion a creeper sitting 3.3-3.5 blocks away — unable to path up onto the platform, but visible to `dangerscan` across the gap — kept `danger.state` pinned at `"panic"` continuously, which appears to hold `REFLEX` from ever handing control back to `PROJECT`: every project set after the 3rd death sat with `task:null` indefinitely, never even attempting a move.

Result: DEAD RACE = DEAD STOP invoked by the driver, ~19 consecutive dead minutes, DNF at stone_pickaxe despite a clean 3m42s wooden pickaxe earlier in the same run. Full narrative in `bots/SCOREBOARD.md`'s run #3 conclusion; raw finding in `bots/FEEDBACK.md` (2026-09-02 test-driver entry).

Also separately noted, not yet explained: 24 cobblestone was mined at 19:42:09 but WALL_OFF reported `kit_violation: no filler blocks` at 19:46:34 with no logged consumption in between — possible inventory-accounting gap, flagging rather than guessing.

## Decider behavior (related, not root cause)
The decider answered every `project_stalled` episode promptly (not the #95 give-up pattern) but re-dispatched the IDENTICAL `chopTrees{types:['oak'],maxDist:32}` three times in a row from a position that never moved, rather than repositioning after the first repeat failure.

## Proposed fixes
1. Generalize the "stuck, no legal path" detector so it isn't underground-scoped — e.g. if N consecutive project attempts across ANY skill produce zero position delta and zero task start, promote to ESCAPE (or a new rung) regardless of y-level/`surfaceExposed`.
2. Decider retry logic should track "did this exact skill+args already fail from this exact position" and reposition (or escalate with a distinct `why`) instead of re-dispatching an identical failing call.
3. `danger.state` staying pinned at `"panic"` against a threat that cannot path to the bot blocks REFLEX indefinitely — a reachability check before an unreachable-but-visible threat holds the ladder hostage would close this. (Also noted: `danger.state` read `"panic"` at score 2.59, below the documented `>=5` panic threshold in DRIVER_GUIDE.md — worth reconciling.)
4. Consider whether vanilla's respawn-point relocation (triggered by the bot's own mining/chopping disturbing the original spawn's safety) should be guarded against landing on a floating/unsupported block at all.

## Specimen
`RotzRudi` process left running (not stopped) on port 3180, world-race3/25600, position (-2.5,109,~4.4) — offered to engine-dev-3 as a live specimen for building the missing surface/elevated-platform escape capability, same pattern as OhneHoseOtto's underground case (#89).

2598	identical `chopTrees{types:oak,maxDist:32}` dispatches from a frozen position. Design choice:
2599	track, per bot, the position+why+lastError signature at the moment of the LAST dispatch
2600	attempt (`state.lastAttempt[bot]`). Before consulting rules.json OR spending an Andy call for
2601	a new episode, compare the CURRENT position+why+lastError against it. If all three are
2602	unchanged (bot hasn't moved, same stall reason, same underlying error) -- nothing observable
2603	about the situation has changed since the last attempt -- skip the decision entirely (saves
2604	the LLM call too, not just the wasted dispatch) and close the episode via **the SAME
2605	`dirClose` API #95 already built** (`closedBy:'frozen_repeat'`), rather than either
2606	blindly re-dispatching an identical failing call or leaving the episode open. This reuses
2607	existing, already-verified machinery (dirClose + reopen backoff) instead of inventing new
2608	agenda-side taxonomy -- deliberately the NARROW fix, not #95's held items 2/3 (a more
2609	specific `why`, RESTOCK's own repeat-count fed into direction). Test-driver's field evidence
2610	here is real and independent of soak #3, but I'm not treating it as grounds to unilaterally
2611	unhold those two bigger, agenda-side changes -- that's still team-lead's call once soak #3's
2612	numbers are in, per their explicit ruling on #95. This is decider.js-only, low blast radius,
2613	verifiable in isolation the same way SOAK_BOT was (no live bot needed to prove the tracking
2614	logic, only the wiring into a real dispatch needs a live check).
2615	
2616	**Item 2 (generalize stuck/ESCAPE detection beyond underground) -- deferring, not building
2617	blind.** Two reasons, both real, not just caution theater:
2618	1. **No live specimen anymore.** RotzRudi had already self-recovered onto real ground by the
2619	   time I looked (test-driver's own manual `come` intervention worked before I started
2620	   diagnosis) -- there is currently no live bot anywhere in the fleet actually stuck on an
2621	   isolated platform to verify a fix against, the same problem #54's fix avoided by using
2622	   KrachKuddel's preserved staged wedge. A staged fixture is buildable (I did exactly this for

2625	   is safety-critical.** `ESCAPE`'s existing act() (`ascendToSurface`) is wrong for this case
2626	   -- the bot is already at/above the surface; going UP doesn't help. The only thing that
2627	   COULD help with zero inventory is a controlled, deliberate fall onto real ground, accepting
2628	   survivable damage (Minecraft fall damage is safe up to 3 blocks, then ~1 HP/block beyond

attempt (`state.lastAttempt[bot]`). Before consulting rules.json OR spending an Andy call for
a new episode, compare the CURRENT position+why+lastError against it. If all three are
unchanged (bot hasn't moved, same stall reason, same underlying error) -- nothing observable
about the situation has changed since the last attempt -- skip the decision entirely (saves
the LLM call too, not just the wasted dispatch) and close the episode via **the SAME
`dirClose` API #95 already built** (`closedBy:'frozen_repeat'`), rather than either
blindly re-dispatching an identical failing call or leaving the episode open. This reuses
existing, already-verified machinery (dirClose + reopen backoff) instead of inventing new
agenda-side taxonomy -- deliberately the NARROW fix, not #95's held items 2/3 (a more
specific `why`, RESTOCK's own repeat-count fed into direction). Test-driver's field evidence
here is real and independent of soak #3, but I'm not treating it as grounds to unilaterally
unhold those two bigger, agenda-side changes -- that's still team-lead's call once soak #3's
numbers are in, per their explicit ruling on #95. This is decider.js-only, low blast radius,
verifiable in isolation the same way SOAK_BOT was (no live bot needed to prove the tracking
logic, only the wiring into a real dispatch needs a live check).

**Item 2 (generalize stuck/ESCAPE detection beyond underground) -- deferring, not building
blind.** Two reasons, both real, not just caution theater:
1. **No live specimen anymore.** RotzRudi had already self-recovered onto real ground by the
   time I looked (test-driver's own manual `come` intervention worked before I started
   diagnosis) -- there is currently no live bot anywhere in the fleet actually stuck on an
   isolated platform to verify a fix against, the same problem #54's fix avoided by using
   KrachKuddel's preserved staged wedge. A staged fixture is buildable (I did exactly this for
   #54's `reposition-cleanstate.sh`), but this needs to happen BEFORE the fix ships, not after.
2. **Detection alone doesn't close the gap -- the missing piece is an ACTION, and that action
   is safety-critical.** `ESCAPE`'s existing act() (`ascendToSurface`) is wrong for this case
   -- the bot is already at/above the surface; going UP doesn't help. The only thing that
   COULD help with zero inventory is a controlled, deliberate fall onto real ground, accepting
   survivable damage (Minecraft fall damage is safe up to 3 blocks, then ~1 HP/block beyond
   that -- RotzRudi's actual 5-6 block drop would have cost roughly 2-3 HP, comfortably
   survivable at the health it had). But `findRepositionTarget`'s existing candidate search
   (the SAME one `_reposition`/ESCAPE already use) only scans `by+1` down to `by-3` --  a
   5-block window that would NOT have found RotzRudi's actual landing spot at all, so this
   isn't a matter of relaxing `surfaceExposed`'s gate on the EXISTING mechanism; it needs a
   genuinely new search (find the nearest edge with an ACCEPTABLE-damage drop within some
   travel radius, verify the landing isn't lava/void/a mob's melee range) and a new skill to
   execute it. A wrong fall-damage calculation, or a landing check that misses standing water
   vs. lava, is the kind of bug that KILLS the bot it's meant to save -- worth building
   carefully against a real staged repro, not shipping from reasoning alone. **Proposing, for
   whoever picks this up next (myself included, once I've staged the fixture) rather than
   building now**: a new `emergencyDescend`-class skill (survivable-fall search + execute),
   triggered by a NEW, underground-independent detection arm on ESCAPE (or a sibling rung) that
   fires when N consecutive project-start attempts across ANY skill produce zero position delta
   and zero task start -- matching test-driver's own suggested detector shape exactly, just
   without the `surfaceExposed` gate. Will stage the fixture and come back to this rather than
   leave it as a permanent gap.

what: engine-dev-3 flagged `logs/metrics-RotzRudi.jsonl` (real gear-race run #3, ~17:46:23Z-17:47:05Z):
`panic phase:'recovered' branch:'WALL_OFF'` firing in extremely tight succession (six within one logged
second at 17:46:53Z) with `danger` re-entering panic immediately after each declared "recovered", three
real `death` events inside 30 seconds.

**Confirmed mechanism, same signature as #94's own diagnostic method applied to this new ledger**: every
one of these `enter`->`recovered` cycles resolves in 20-30ms (e.g. 17:46:53.512->17:46:53.539 = 27ms) —
exactly the same "too fast to be real construction" fingerprint #94 measured across 593 cycles. Cross-
referenced against `task_end` records: cobblestone was genuinely mined (24 at 17:42:09, +1 at 17:42:51,
+1 at 17:44:58 — 26 total, never replenished again before the death sequence at 17:46:23+). Engine-dev-3
independently confirmed via their own #97 investigation that WALL_OFF legitimately spent this filler
across ~2 real seal attempts earlier in the same encounter, not a leak. By the time we reach THIS ledger
segment, filler is exhausted, and every subsequent `branchWallOff` call hits the same synchronous
`fillerItem()` no-filler bail #94 found — zero real construction, zero protection, ~20-30ms per cycle,
while the attacking mob keeps landing real hits every cycle.

**Why #94's fix does NOT cover this case — the actually new part of this finding**: `pick()` only ever
reaches `branchBreakLOS` (where #94's corner-step fix lives) via its `ranged && los` check. RotzRudi's
attacker throughout this segment is consistent with a MELEE threat (danger's own `threats` entries in
this window carry no `ranged:true`) — `pick()` never routes a melee threat through BREAK_LOS at all. The
melee `FLEE_HOME` path requires `bot.health >= 6`; once HP crossed below that (5.33 -> 2.83 -> 0.33 across
this exact segment), that gate closes too, and `pick()` falls straight to `branchWallOff(nearest)` with
**no intermediate branch, no corner-step opportunity, nothing #94 touches**. A melee attacker against a
sub-6-HP, filler-less bot has ZERO possible active defense today, by construction — not a bug in any one
branch, but a genuine gap in the routing table itself.

**This is #96, field-confirmed, not hypothetical.** #96 (filed today, "last-resort defense for a
genuinely unkitted bot") was framed around QA-fixture evidence with an open question — "may be testing a
state well-kitted bots practically never enter." This incident answers that question: a real fleet bot,
mid-race, doing completely ordinary things (mining pickaxe upgrades, producing sticks/torches) ran its
filler down over the course of a normal encounter and hit this exact ceiling live, three times, fatally.
Updating #96 with this evidence rather than filing a duplicate — the design question it already poses
(filler-independent last resort vs. leaning harder on kit-preflight/mid-encounter resupply awareness) is
the same question, now with a body count instead of a fixture number.

**Not fixed here, deliberately**: this needs a real design decision (does corner-step's LOS-breaking
value generalize usefully to melee threats too, despite melee not caring about sightlines the way a
skeleton's arrows do? does FLEE_HOME's `health>=6` gate need an exception when the alternative is
provably zero defense? does WALL_OFF need to warn a driver/decider BEFORE filler actually runs out rather
than only reporting the violation after the fact?) rather than a narrow one-line patch like #94/#98 — per
this file's own "argue before building" doctrine, that argument belongs on #96 as a maintainer decision,
not something to rush from a teammate flag mid-soak.

## What happened

Felix caught this live in-game (screenshot, 25599) during KrachKuddel's/KrachKarla's chopTrees
work: the skill left a tree half-felled -- a floating remainder of the trunk/canopy still
standing -- with the wood drops sitting ON TOP of the remaining leaves rather than on the
ground.

This violates two standing project laws at once:
1. **Never-leave-drops**: drops elevated on top of leaf blocks are invisible to (and
   unreachable by) a ground-level collectDrops sweep -- they're lost the same as if they'd
   never dropped, and per the project's own doctrine, rival bots/players can snipe visible
   drops in seconds regardless.
2. **Aesthetics / "no half-eaten trees"**: this is the literal example the aesthetics law
   names as the thing not to do -- a human player fells a whole tree, not a stump with a
   floating canopy remnant.

## Likely mechanism (not yet diagnosed in code -- filing from the field observation first,
per team-lead's instruction to file now and fix after #101)

Two candidate causes, not mutually exclusive:
- The skill doesn't fell the WHOLE trunk column in one pass -- it may stop once it judges
  the "trunk" portion done, leaving upper trunk/canopy blocks (and the leaves they support)
  unfelled.
- Vanilla behavior: chopping a tree from below can leave leaf drops resting on remaining
  leaf blocks above where they fell, which a ground-level-only collection sweep never
  reaches.

## Suggested fix directions (not built -- this is a report)

1. Fell the whole trunk column the skill already knows the tree's blocks for -- finish the
   job rather than stopping partway.
2. Either collect drops AT canopy height (before/during felling, not only after from the
   ground), or change the felling order so drops can never end up resting on unfelled
   leaves in the first place (e.g., top-down felling instead of bottom-up).

## Status

Filed per team-lead's instruction (Felix's live screenshot, real gear-race/soak fleet
activity). #101 (craftToolChain table-placement retry, soak #4 blocker) and the R2 wedge
diagnosis it's currently sequenced behind take priority; this is queued as an independent
follow-up in the same lane (skills.js).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
=====103=====
**Finding, from gear-race run #5 (SCOREBOARD.md, Engine Gear-Race section, BruzzelBruno):** the bot died once, organically, to a zombie, with the `#96` zero-defense floor firing correctly. Post-respawn: clean respawn, HP/food full, `agenda` cleared to `IDLE` with no project — and it just sat there for the rest of the run. No re-arm was ever issued; the run was suspended by an operator wind-down before anyone (driver or engine) acted on it. A `/state` snapshot of "just died, never re-armed" looks identical at a glance to "calm and fine between two legitimate task phases" — both read `task:null`, `hp:20/20`. That ambiguity, not the death itself, is the actual gap.

**Why the existing machinery doesn't catch this promptly:** `unproductive_idle` (research/IDLE_TRIGGER_SPEC.md's episode-trigger table) would *eventually* open on this bot — "no project, no task in flight, nothing graded productive for 120s" — but that's a minimum 2-minute blind spot, and it only catches death-then-idle *by inference*, the same way it catches every other flavor of stall. A death is a much stronger, more precise signal than that: it's directly observable at the exact moment it happens, not something that has to be inferred from an absence of productivity two minutes later.

**The hook points already exist, they just aren't wired to Direction Episodes:**
- `runner.js:524-525` — `bot.on('death', ...)` already fires on every death, today, purely for a log line + reconnect bookkeeping.
- `runner.js:473-476` — `bot.on('spawn', ...)` already re-runs the full payload stack on every spawn "including death-respawn" (that comment's own words), which is what clears the active project in the first place.

So the moment agenda's state goes idle-with-no-project because of a death is already a moment the runtime observes directly — nothing needs to be inferred, and no new detection mechanism needs to be built from scratch.

**Proposed fix direction (framed as a Direction Episodes edge trigger, per team-lead's steer):** a death/respawn is the purest possible `needs_direction` moment there is — the bot is *provably* projectless and idle, not probably. Add a new episode `why` (e.g. `respawned`) opened directly from the death/spawn hook path above, alongside the existing `project_done` / `project_blocked` / `no_tool` / `unproductive_idle` / `project_stalled` triggers in agenda.js's direction machinery — instead of waiting for the generic `unproductive_idle` window to eventually notice. The decider/driver then answers a `respawned` episode exactly like any other open episode (a role-based bot's normal `ROLE_WORK` re-arm, a role-less bot's race-book branch, or a generic "re-arm from scratch" default) — closing the death-to-rearm gap to near-zero with no race-specific or death-specific logic anywhere except the one new trigger.

**Precedent, cross-referenced:** this is the same shape as `#88` (role:null bots had zero food-acquisition path because nothing routed a food shortfall to an answerable trigger — closed by making the shortfall decider-visible instead of relying on inference). Same fix pattern, applied to death instead of hunger.

**Not blocking anything today:** gear-race run #6 carries a manual driver-side mitigation for this in the meantime (Race book v2, SCOREBOARD.md, "Combat-loss-at-night branch" — detect the death line, read-only inventory check, re-arm from scratch, log the death-to-rearm gap as its own timed metric). This issue is the engine-side follow-up so future runs (and the fleet generally) don't need a driver watching for it by hand.

**Owner:** agenda.js lane (engine-dev-3), no urgency — later, not gating run #6.

Filed by test-driver, night shift, 2026-09-02.

=====90=====
Tracking issue for the "Engine Gear-Race" benchmark series (SCOREBOARD.md), since it's become a recurring, findings-generating measurement (two runs so far, `bench/gearrace.mjs` now automates it) rather than a one-off — filing per team-lead's request rather than leaving it as SCOREBOARD-only.

## Format

Driverless engine, steered ONLY via `setProject` (no hand-driving, no `/eval` action code, no depot/RCON help). Score = wall-clock from server-log join to first possession of each pickaxe tier (wooden/stone/iron/diamond); steering-call count is a secondary autonomy metric. Run cap 90 min. Automated by `bench/gearrace.mjs` (ground truth: server log join line + `Tool ready` chat lines, corroborated by the ledger's `inv` snapshots; steering-call count from the ledger's `intervention` events — the harness makes zero `/eval` calls of its own).

## Runs so far

- **Run #0 — NacktNorbert, shared/contaminated 25599 world.** Shakedown, not comparable (deforested spawn area). Wooden pickaxe T+6m19s after two failed wood-searches; surfaced the #86 plank-churn bug and the harvestGrass-without-`repeat` footgun. Concluded on purpose (no-loiter law) once findings were extracted, never hit a genuine dead end.
- **Run #1 — OhneHoseOtto, dedicated virgin 25600 track (same seed) — OFFICIAL BASELINE.** Wooden pickaxe clean at T+1m00s. **DNF at stone.** Official cause: (a) the food-item kit shortfall was un-actionable by the ladder — `huntAnimals`'s own gate is clean (#45, verified live) but nothing routed a food shortfall to hunting automatically; (b) **terminal** — while mining toward stone the bot sealed itself in a pocket at y89 with no path to food, fauna, or the surface. Now handed off live as the `digOut`/ascendToSurface specimen (#89) — DO NOT rescue it.

Full timestamped narrative for both runs lives in SCOREBOARD.md's "Engine Gear-Race" section; do not duplicate it here, link forward from future runs instead.

## Green-light criteria for run #2 (per team-lead's ruling, 2026-09-02)

The gate itself (#45) is fine and is NOT part of this checklist. What must land first, both required (run #2 measures the delta against run #1's two diagnosed failure modes):
- [x] **Food-routing fix** — some agenda rung automatically routes a food shortfall to `huntAnimals`/`harvestGrass` instead of requiring a driver to notice and branch manually. Landed: agenda v20, commit 1acc849 (`ROLE_WORK.hunter -> huntAnimals`, composes with #84's `effectiveKit`). Live-verified: 148/148 preflight, fresh bot (EngineDreckDave/3150).
- [ ] **`digOut`/`ascendToSurface` skill** (#89) landing and being verified against the OhneHoseOtto specimen.

Race book v1 (pre-planned setProject sequence per tier, known-failure branch plans, and the "DEAD RACE = DEAD STOP" 5-minute rule) is already written in SCOREBOARD.md for whoever drives run #2 — no need to re-derive it here.

## Open housekeeping

- `bench/gearrace.mjs`'s `ADVANCEMENT_MAP` dispute (whether `Isn't It Iron Pick?` maps to iron or diamond) is resolved (diamond is correct; `story/iron_tools` is the real iron-pickaxe advancement) — the harness never used advancement titles for timing either way, so no historical data is affected.

Cross-reference: #89 (digOut specimen + skill), #45/#84 (closed, the two routing fixes this race's baseline exposed), #64 (roadmap CONTINUE decision this benchmark series informs).

## Finding

Found during a wait-filler composition-rot sweep (audit-only, per team-lead's standing authority — full trace in FEEDBACK.md, 2026-09-02, "wait-filler sweep #2"). Same family as #38 ("phantom instruments" — a signal that looks the same whether it fired for real or not) and today's own doctrine: "assumed false" and "verified false" must be distinguishable downstream, or code inherits invisible uncertainty.

`dangerscan.js`'s `scan()` computes line-of-sight via a real raycast (`hasLOS`) for each hostile/mob candidate, nearest-first, but bounds itself to `g.thresholds.maxRaycasts` (currently 8) per scan tick. Once that budget is exhausted, the code says outright what happens (its own comment): `// budget spent: assume no LOS rather than skipping the threat`. Every remaining candidate that tick gets `los: false` in its `threats[]` entry — not because a raycast confirmed no line of sight, but because none was attempted.

Nothing downstream — notably `survival.js`'s `pick()`, whose `BREAK_LOS` routing is gated on `ranged && los` — has any way to tell an assumed-false `los` from a genuinely-verified one; both look identical in the `threats[]` array. A real skeleton (or stray/witch/bogged) beyond the 8th-nearest hostile within the 24-block scan radius, that genuinely has line of sight on the bot, would be silently treated as not-visible and never routed to `BREAK_LOS` — falling through toward `FLEE_HOME`/`WALL_OFF`/`FIGHT_BACK`/`FLEE_AWAY` instead, none of which are built for "corner-step or arrow-shadow against a ranged attacker that's actually shooting."

## Scope, stated honestly

Narrower than today's other survival-lane findings:
- **Trigger condition**: needs more than 8 simultaneous hostile/mob entities within 24 blocks — a mob farm, a crowded night-surface spawn, a horde event. Not an everyday single-attacker encounter.
- **Mitigating factor**: candidates are processed nearest-first, so the closest (most dangerous) threats always get a real raycast; a budget-exhausted assumption only ever affects farther, lower-priority candidates.

## Proposed fix (not built — no live sighting yet, per the "no build without one" standard this session has been holding to)

Cheap: tag budget-exhausted entries with an explicit `losAssumed: true` field — free, since the information already exists at the exact point `los` is assigned (`else los = ranged ? 0.3 : 0.6;`), just discarded today. That alone doesn't change behavior; it gives `pick()` or a future refinement the option to treat "assumed false" differently from "verified false" without dangerscan needing to spend more raycasts than its own budget allows.

## Evidence

===54 body===
## Roadmap · Arc A · Movement RECOVERY LADDER (ordered escalation rungs) · Milestone M2 — build AFTER the shakeout

**Decision this serves:** the keystone acceptance-BLOCKING build. Without it, **criterion #5 is unpassable** (the only current answer to a wedge is a manual RCON teleport — the last human-in-the-loop crutch) and **criterion #1** is at risk. The recovery ladder stays **100% deterministic** — an LLM in the per-tick recovery loop would violate the codicil and the `tokensSpent=0` bar.

**Sequencing (applied from critique):** build the DETECTION layer first (sibling issue), run the shakeout, then build **only the escalation rungs the wedge distribution justifies**. Do not pre-implement all eight rungs blind.

### Ordered escalating recovery ladder (ROS Nav2 recovery-behavior pattern; cheapest/safest first)
- **R0** re-verify arrival (false-reached check — maybe we DID arrive).
- **R1** generalized `_unstick` (see detection issue) + jump-back x3.
- **R2** reposition to nearest safe standing cell and re-issue.
- **R3** replan-from-current with a **virtual-obstacle blacklist** so A* never re-derives the failing path.
- **R4** goal relaxation (GoalNear → GoalNearXZ tolerance ladder, reachable-waypoint fallback).
- **R5** macro self-rescue (dig-to-goal / pillar-up / bridge-gap) — GATED, always routed through digguard/toolguard/reachguard so recovery never scars terrain or violates a claim. **Kept OFF the acceptance-critical path until placeBlock (#19) is hardened** — R5 rests on placeBlock, the flakiest primitive in the stack (silent no-op on hitbox overlap #19, false blockUpdate timeouts). Do not let the recovery-of-last-resort depend on the least-reliable foundation.
- **R6** relog (drives the payload re-inject; attempt-capped).
- **R7** teleport (RCON) — the **LAST** rung; every firing writes a **"recovery-ladder MISS" to FEEDBACK.md**.

### Corrupt-chunk freeze (#20 — the CRITICAL that forced the only manual tp)
Detectable signature: `blockAt` air at feet/head/below + `onGround:true` + tiny `-y` velocity. Wire as a first-class stall class → capped relog → escalate to a **logged R7 teleport with a hard alarm**. The watchdog only DETECTS it; only relog CURES it — ship both together. **Adjudication (applied from critique):** corrupt-chunk is a **survivability + alarm** case, **not** a criterion-#5 self-recovery proof (RCON tp is an out-of-band admin escape hatch; counting it as self-recovery would be recovery-determinism-theater).

### Depot-less inventory-saturation rung (added from critique — missing coverage)
The strongest evidence run was **depot-less and deep**; over hours the bot's own inventory fills with cobble/dirt, silently breaking drop pickup and mineLane's banked-count math. Add a rung/heuristic that sheds or halts on **self-inventory pressure** in the depot-less soak config (distinct from depot-chest overfill #15).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A **deliberately induced IN-WORLD wedge** (torch-underfoot / ledge / boundary-bounce) resumes driverless with **zero intervention**, resolved at **R6-or-below**. Any R7/RCON firing on that fixture counts as a **criterion-#5 MISS**.
- [ ] An induced corrupt-chunk signature (#20) resolves via capped relog → logged R7 + alarm (treated as survivability, not #5 proof).
- [ ] Teleport fires **only** as R7 and logs a FEEDBACK miss each time; rung-firing frequency is emitted as a first-class soak metric and **trends down** across successive soaks (a ladder that fires constantly is a red flag, not a win).
- [ ] Depot-less inventory-saturation rung verified in the depot-less config.
- [ ] `bench/preflight.sh` 55/55 green.

### Execution-loop guarantees ported from Baritone (imitate as tuned JS — treat as NEW engineering, not constant-tuning)
Per-move tick budget scaled to expected cost; cost re-verification (cancel+replan); off-path drift bailout; virtual-obstacle blacklist; replan-from-current. These come from tick-level movement control pathfinder does not expose — budget them as real work. Tune EMPIRICALLY on the shakeout.

### Relevant files / targets
- `skills.js` (`ctx.goto`, recovery ladder), `agenda.js` (stall class routing), `runner.js` (relog/backoff, RCON path), `digguard.js`, `FEEDBACK.md`
- Consolidates the recovery aspects of: #20, #33, #34, #2, #29, #38.

### Lane
Core (engine-dev-2). Depends on the detection layer + the shakeout.

content.content:
=== 96 comments ===
**Field-confirmed, not just hypothetical — this killed a real gear-race bot three times.**

engine-dev-3 flagged `logs/metrics-RotzRudi.jsonl` (real gear-race run #3, ~17:46:23Z-17:47:05Z): `WALL_OFF` firing in extremely tight succession (six within one logged second) with three real deaths inside 30 seconds. Diagnosed it: same sub-30ms no-filler bail signature #94 measured (593 cycles, 99% under 100ms) — cross-referenced against `task_end` records, cobblestone was genuinely mined (26 total) and legitimately spent on ~2 real seal attempts earlier in the same encounter (engine-dev-3 independently confirmed this, not a leak). By the time of the triple-death, filler was exhausted, and every subsequent `branchWallOff` call hit the same synchronous no-filler bail — zero protection, ~20-30ms per cycle, real hits landing every cycle.

**The new part**: #94's fix doesn't cover this case. `pick()` only reaches `branchBreakLOS` (where #94's corner-step fix lives) via a `ranged && los` check — RotzRudi's attacker here is melee. The melee `FLEE_HOME` path requires `health>=6`; once HP dropped below that, `pick()` fell straight to `branchWallOff(nearest)` with no intermediate branch and no corner-step opportunity at all. **A melee attacker against a sub-6-HP, filler-less bot has zero possible active defense today, by construction — a gap in the routing table, not a bug in one branch.**

This answers this issue's own open question ("may be testing a state well-kitted bots practic
--- end 96 ---
=== 98 comments ===
**Fixed and verified (skills.js v59, survival.js v8, commit 21f7d98).**

`S.reachOf = _reachOf;` exposed in skills.js (zero new logic — the exact existing probe, made callable from another payload). `pick()`'s FLEE_HOME routing in survival.js now gates on `homeReachable()` (calls `S.reachOf(bot, g.home)`, fails open if skills.js isn't installed) before committing, falling through to `branchWallOff` when home isn't actually reachable.

No regression: full preflight 199/199, `survival-cannotheal.js` still 7/7 (#92 untouched).

Both directions live-verified with a new fixture (`bench/fixtures/flee-home-reachability.sh`): built two real geometries at the same straight-line distance class — an open connected platform and a fully sealed box — same fabricated melee threat both times, triggered the real `enter()`/`pick()`. Home reachable → FLEE_HOME with ~2.1s of genuine travel (unchanged). Home sealed off → falls through to WALL_OFF in 10-48ms instead of burning the full 30s finding out. 2/2 repeat runs, both clean.

One honest note for anyone else testing FLEE_HOME on the local server: `protected.json`'s configured home is literally floating air there (the real base only exists on production) — worked around it by overriding `__survival.home` to a real built platform for the test rather than assuming the configured value corresponds to actual terrain.

--- end 98 ---
=== 99 comments ===
**Ledger size warning for whoever mines this** (team-lead's flag): SabberSepp is being left running as a live specimen and the bug is still actively thrashing, so its ledgers are growing continuously and are already large:
- `logs/metrics-SabberSepp.jsonl`: 1.0MB / 5700 lines as of 20:38
- `logs/SabberSepp.log`: 433KB / 3807 lines as of 20:38

Both will keep growing for as long as the specimen is left alive and thrashing (the loop fires roughly every 0.3-1s). Anyone querying/grepping these should expect them to be substantially larger by the time they look, and should probably `tail`/seek rather than read the whole file, or ask the driver to pause/stop the specimen first if a full-file read is needed.
## Diagnosed and fixed live

Confirmed the exact mechanism via direct introspection on SabberSepp (not guessed from the
log alone): `__survival.brief()` showed `branch:'WALL_OFF'`, fires climbing unbounded
(2060+ and rising), `standdown:null`, while `__survival.cannotHeal()` independently
evaluated `true` at that moment (food:17 < regen floor 18, no food item held).

**Root cause**: `branchWallOff`'s `if (!fillerItem())` early bail (before it even attempts a
seal) returns `{ branch: 'WALL_OFF', sealed: false, reason: 'no_filler' }` with **no
`cannotHeal` field**. `enter()`'s existing #92 standdown-arming check
(`out.branch==='WALL_OFF' && out.cannotHeal`) only ever sees that field set by the FULL
seal-attempt path further down the same function — it silently never fires for th
--- end 99 ---
=== 100 comments ===
**Fixed and verified (survival.js v10, commit 2fc5234 — landed alongside a concurrent decider.js commit via a staging-area race, same benign pattern as #99 earlier today; contents verified intact and correct).**

`enter()`'s standdown-arming is now `dangerSettled = out.branch !== 'ENV' && threatsNow().length === 0 && !(out.branch === 'FLEE_AWAY' && out.cornered)`, armed alongside `cannotHeal()` regardless of which branch produced the outcome.

Walked every branch for suppression risk before building, per the ask, and found two real exclusions rather than shipping the literal predicate unmodified:
- **ENV excluded**: `branchEnv` never verifies its hazard is actually resolved, and `pick()`'s own first check on every call is `envHazard()` — arming standdown here could suppress that recheck for the one branch class whose whole point is "nothing else matters."
- **FLEE_AWAY's own `cornered:true` excluded**: not hypothetical — #94's diagnosis already found dangerscan's threat list can read empty while a real melee attacker is still adjacent (the "self-blinding" observation from RotzRudi's ledger). Arming right after the one branch whose own result says "did not actually get away" risks exactly that.

No regression: full preflight 203/203, `flee-home-reachability.sh` still PASS.

Verified precisely, not just observed: added 3 new cases to `survival-cannotheal.js` (now 11/11) using `g.drill()` to force each predicate outcome directly — `ENV` (fabricated hazard) correctly stay
--- end 100 ---
=== 101 comments ===
Fixed and verified — skills.js v60, commit cd30f4c (+ FEEDBACK.md log 0820498).

**Fix**: new `seekPlaceableSpot()` in skills.js — an expanding square-ring search (bounded by `TERRAIN_SEEK_RADIUS=10`, "cheap stone-tool travel law" per team-lead's ruling) for genuinely walkable ground (solid below, clear feet/head — matches `findRepositionTarget`'s own standability test, not `placeCarriedTable`'s reach-based "air with a solid face" test — conflating those two was my first wrong draft). `craftToolChain` now walks there via `gotoT` and retries `placeCarriedTable()` once a spot is found, instead of giving up on the exact cell the bot happens to be stuck on. Built as a reusable primitive (not a one-off patch) per team-lead's ruling — #97 item 2's eventual generalized "no legal path" recovery wants this same search, and it already reuses `_reachOf`/`S.reachOf` (#70) to order candidates, which is exactly the idiom engine-dev's #98 fix (`survival.js:829`) predicted "eng-3's #97 fix is expected to want... from a different file." A genuinely marooned bot still fails honestly and fast once the radius is exhausted.

**Fixture**: `bench/fixtures/craft-terrain-seek.sh` (new) rebuilds the real pillar geometry via RCON and proves both directions — a solvable isolated pillar must succeed via the new path (steps show `terrain-seek:...:placed`), a genuinely marooned one must fail fast and honestly. 10/10 standalone runs, holds inside the full tier0 suite, `preflight.sh` 203/203 clea
--- end 101 ---

the local server, 8/8 clean after two fixture-construction bugs found and fixed along the

2. `MET().recovery('R2', n)` emits into a telemetry sink that doesn't exist — `telemetry.js` has no `recovery` method, so the `m && m.recovery` guard is permanently false and every R2 firing is invisible to the ledger. Cross-reference #69: same failure class as `M.chest()` (defined, never called), opposite direction (called, sink never defined).
3. **The branch is the real hazard, not the code.** `main..hunt-gate-45` looks 4 commits ahead but 3 of those (#45/#67a/#67b) are already on main as separate cherry-picks git doesn't recognise as the same work, while `hunt-gate-45..main` is 20+ commits behind (including #70/#71/#72/#73-75) on a `skills.js` three engine versions stale. Merging would silently revert #70's reachability filter or #71's charcoal path onto the live fleet. Verdict: cherry-pick `44d4bed` only, never merge the branch.

R2 stays OFF the fleet until those three land. Prediction on record for whenever #57's soak produces the wedge distribution: the REPOSITION term will be low-yield relative to the re-issued A* (dead-reckons `forward`+`jump` without checking what's between here and there), which if borne out argues for simplifying the rung rather than tuning it.

Cross-reference: #70 (closed, measurement precedent), #27 (swallowed cancellation), #69 (ledger sink gaps).
telemetry.js side of this closed: `M.recovery(rung, attempt, extra)` now exists (commit b9ccd20), so `MET().recovery('R2', n)` in gotoR's catch block (landed as f6adce8) fires into a real sink instead of a permanently-false guard. `gid` links back to the FAILED goto span (`M.goto` is already cleared by the time the caller's catch runs, so `gotoEnd` now stashes `M._lastGotoGid` first). `metrics.mjs` has a new "recovery ladder" section: firing frequency by rung, paired with the immediately-following `goto` record (the retry's own outcome, via seq order — gotoR's control flow is strictly sequential so no bespoke join key is needed).

Also proposed (not yet applied — skills.js is engine-dev-3's lane) a one-line, purely-additive change to the gotoR catch block: call `_reposition()` first and pass its boolean as `{displaced}`. That's the field needed to score eng-2's on-record review prediction ("the re-issued A* is where the wins come from, not the reposition") — metrics.mjs already reports the split (`retry-arrived with displaced=true: N vs false: N`) whenever the field is present, and degrades gracefully when it's absent.

Separately: wrote `bench/fixtures/wedge-r2-twin-doorway.sh`, a proposed (NOT YET RUN — server down all session) live fixture for the half `gotoR-recovery.js`'s own header says it can't prove — that R2 actually resolves a genuine wedge, not just that the candidate search is correct in isolation. Full design + honest uncertainty in FEEDBACK.md (2026-09-02 entries). Queued behind the server coming back up; flagged as a joint task with engine-dev-3.
**#54-R2 landed on main (engine-dev-3, f6adce8), the required fixes applied, R2 stays OFF the fleet pending live wedge resolution.**

Cherry-picked `44d4bed` onto main rather than merging `hunt-gate-45` — verified by reading both diff directions that 3 of the branch's 4 commits (#45/#67a/#67b) are already on main as unrecognized cherry-picks and the branch sat 26 commits behind at v43 vs main's v47. Clean auto-merge, resolved against v47.

Applied the required fix: `_reposition`'s `catch (_) {}` now rethrows on `e && e.cancelled` instead of swallowing the `Cancelled` sentinel — a dying reposition no longer finishes its 1.5s walk out from under a preempting rung (survival flee etc.), same shape as #27.

Also closed half of "R2 resolves a wedge is unproven": extracted `_reposition`'s candidate-cell search into a pure `findRepositionTarget`, exposed as `S.recoveryDetect` (same discipline as `S.moveDetect` from #53 — "a rule testable only by staging the bug does not stay tested"). `bench/fixtures/gotoR-recovery.js` proves the search picks the right cell in the right priority order, protection-respecting — it does NOT and cannot prove walking there actually unwedges a real pathfinder.

Timing analysis (worked from the actual FROZEN/NO_PROGRESS constants): a pure FROZEN wedge reaches `stuck` in ~25-30s, comfortably inside `gotoNear`'s own 30s default; NO_PROGRESS needs ~60-66s, past every caller's budget including the 60s-timeout ones. So NO_PROGRESS essentially never reaches `stuck` under any timeout this codebase uses — only a genuinely FROZEN, non-diggable-obstruction wedge is a realistic R2 trigger. This is the concrete version of "thinkTimeout pre-empts stuck."

Converged independently with engine-dev on the same session: they built the `M.recovery` sink (b9ccd20, closing the review's ledger gap) and proposed `bench/fixtures/wedge-r2-twin-doorway.sh` — a live geometry trap, written and syntax-checked, NOT run (server down all session). Reviewed it as the gotoR/_reposition owner: sound design, one open empirical question flagged (whether mineflayer-pathfinder's real A* actually thrashes on this shape vs. cleanly finding the open gap — the fixture already treats that as INCONCLUSIVE rather than assuming it works).

Landed the two follow-on patches engine-dev specified for my lane: `M.chest()` wired into all 4 real chest transactions (#69 gap 1, 38e1adc) and `gotoR`'s `{displaced}` field reorder (also 38e1adc) so `metrics.mjs` can score the displaced-vs-replan prediction on record.

Full writeup: FEEDBACK.md, 2026-09-02 entries. R2 stays held off the fleet — live resolution proof needs a server.
Ran the wedge-r2-twin-doorway.sh fixture live against a real bot now that the local server is up. Result: the harness works (fixed three real infra bugs: chunk-load race on teleport, silent /fill no-op on ungenerated chunks, a build_platform "island" gap), but the actual obstruction mechanism is still unsolved after four falsified live attempts:

1. **`minecraft:barrier`**: bot reaches the goal in 4s, zero recovery events. mineflayer-pathfinder's A* is a complete graph search — a block-impassable edge is just excluded from the graph, so it finds the real gap immediately and never tries the blocked one. Nothing for R2 to recover from.
2. **Non-marker `armor_stand`**: reasoned that `entitiesToAvoid` (runner.js) is scoped to hostile mobs only, so the search would price both gaps as open while the entity's hitbox should physically stop the walk. Live-observed: the bot walked straight through it. **mineflayer's client-side physics doesn't simulate entity-vs-entity collision for the bot's own movement at all** — this rules out any entity-based obstruction, not just this one.
3&4. **`cobweb` and `short_dry_grass`** (queried the live registry for leaf_litter-class blocks — empty boundingBox + `shapes:[]` + diggable, not yet in `blocksToAvoid`; 231 matches). Both walked through at full speed with zero stall. Whatever broke onGround/auto-jump for the original torch/leaf_litter bug is specific to those blocks, not a general property shared by same-signature blocks.

Full mechanism-level writeup in the fixture's header (REVISIONS 1-4) and FEEDBACK.md. This narrows the search space materially but does NOT prove R2 resolves a live wedge — the gate is still open. Two untried paths: a genuinely different execution-level failure theory (parkour/jump-timing is closed off since `allowParkour=false`), or instrumenting to catch a NATURALLY occurring wedge during normal fleet operation instead of constructing one synthetically.
**Proof gate re-scoped by team-lead (2026-09-02): synthetic geometry hunting formally stood down.** Five live attempts to construct an R2-triggering wedge on demand were tried and falsified, each with a mechanism-level explanation (full revision history in `bench/fixtures/wedge-r2-twin-doorway.sh`'s own header):
1. `minecraft:barrier` false-lead gap — mineflayer-pathfinder's A* is a complete graph search, so a block-level-impassable edge is simply excluded; the search finds the real gap on the first attempt and never "tries" the blocked one. Nothing for R2 to recover from.
2. Non-marker `armor_stand` in the false-lead gap — LIVE-OBSERVED the bot walked straight through its exact cell. Generalizes: mineflayer's client-side physics does not simulate entity-vs-entity collision for the bot's own movement at all, only block AABBs (filed separately as #87).
3-4. `cobweb` and `short_dry_grass` (same empty-boundingBox signature as the original leaf_litter/torch wedge) — both walked through at full speed, no stall. The original bug was those two blocks' own since-patched quirk, not a general property of the registry's other 231 same-signature blocks.
5. Perpendicular flowing water — inconclusive rather than falsified (the mechanism is still plausible; the specific construction may just not have produced a strong-enough current), timeboxed to one attempt per plan and not pursued further.

**Re-scoped path forward, per team-lead, replacing further synthetic-geometry attempts:** (a) **fault-injection** (engine-dev-3's lane) and (b) **first natural firing in field telemetry**, monitored via the now-real `M.recovery` sink (closed the ledger gap this issue's own R2 review flagged — see the doctrine-sweep entries above) plus the new continuous position trace (#69 gap 2). The gear-race run already produced one naturally-wedged bot (OhneHoseOtto, handed off live for `digOut`/ascendToSurface development, see the new issue for that) — instrumenting real fleet operation for an organic `recovery` firing is judged higher-fidelity than more construction effort on synthetic traps.

Candidate search itself stays proven correct (`findRepositionTarget`/`S.recoveryDetect`, 6 cases, `bench/fixtures/gotoR-recovery.js`) — what's still open is real-wedge resolution end-to-end. Status unchanged from the live-wedge-fixture entries above: R2 stays off cavecrew until a natural or fault-injected firing closes the loop.
**Fault-injection half of the re-scoped gate: PASSED live.** (skills v54, commit 59c843d)

Built the hook exactly as scoped: gotoR's first attempt checks `globalThis.__r2Fault` (armed via /eval before starting a goto-driving skill) and throws a synthetic `stuck` immediately instead of waiting out the real watchdog -- consumed one-shot before the throw. Everything after that is completely real: `ctx._reposition()`'s walk against the actual world, the re-issued A* against actual terrain, whether it actually arrives.

Per #38's doctrine (the last hook of this shape, `drill()`'s `pickOverride`, was silently broken its whole life because nothing verified it fired), this one writes `globalThis.__r2FaultProof` as the episode unfolds and the fixture (`bench/fixtures/wedge-r2-fault-inject.sh`) asserts on TWO independent channels -- the in-process proof object AND the ledger's own `recovery`+`goto` records -- requiring them to agree, not trusting either alone.

Live result (EngineDreckDave/3150, 25599): fired on attempt 0; `_reposition()` genuinely displaced the bot; the re-issued goto was a real 29-block A* search (48 nodes visited, 2 replans) that arrived; the ledger's `recovery` record independently carries `injected:true` and the next `goto` record shows `res:arrived`, matching exactly. Full PASS.

What this proves: R2's resolution mechanism (reposition + fresh A*) works and completes on a live bot when invoked. What it doesn't: that an organic wedge will trigger it -- that's the still-open field half (first naturally-occurring firing-and-resolution in fleet telemetry via the M.recovery sink). Both halves together are the deployable-to-cavecrew standard; this closes the first.

Full writeup: FEEDBACK.md, 2026-09-02.
**First natural (non-injected) R2 firing caught, via the armed monitor.** 10 genuine `recovery` records on FrischFriedhelm (test-driver's active gear-race run #2, no `injected` key present at all — every prior firing this session was engine-dev-3's fault-injection test and always carried `injected:true`).

Full ledger reconstruction (goto/wedge/recovery/task together, not just the recovery events alone): `come` was trying to reach a target ~60+ blocks away with real elevation change. The bot went genuinely FROZEN near (-3,96,5)/(2,101,2), cycled FROZEN→stuck→R2(`displaced:false`)→FROZEN **nine times over 552 seconds (~9.2 min)** — `_reposition()` could not find anywhere to actually move the bot each time, and every one of those retries also ended stuck/path_timeout. The **tenth** firing finally got `displaced:true` (a real 2-block shift), and the fresh A* from the new cell found a clean 64.3-block route to the goal on the first try — `res:"arrived"`.

**Honest headline number** (from `metrics.mjs`'s own recovery-ladder section, run against this real ledger): R2 fired 10 times, resolved once. 10% natural per-firing resolution, not "R2 works" — "R2 eventually works, at real cost, when displacement keeps failing."

This also flips the framing of eng-2's original review prediction: resolutions here cluster overwhelmingly at `displaced:true` (1/1), not `displaced:false` (0/9) — the opposite of "the re-plan does the work regardless of displacement." A fresh A* from the SAME position as a failed one has no reason to find a different answer; displacement looks NECESSARY here, not incidental.

**Real open question, not "does R2 work":** why did `_reposition`'s 8-candidate search return "nowhere to go" nine times running at this location? Open sky at y~96-101 near a possible ledge/cliff is a plausible culprit — unconfirmed, not guessed at further. Deliberately not queried live: FrischFriedhelm is test-driver's active, measured gear-race run, and a diagnostic `/eval` call would contaminate their steering-call count.

Recommend keeping #54 open rather than closing as "proven" — both gate halves now have live evidence, but the natural hit rate at hard geometry doesn't yet look ready to ship silently. Full writeup in FEEDBACK.md (commit 4a1b0ec).
**Staked: exact wild wedge geometry** (per team-lead's directive — pure ledger read, no bot contact, no interference with the still-active gear-race run).

**World**: `/home/felix/minecraft/localserver-race` (port 25600, rcon 25601), level-name `world-race2` (both `world-race` and `world-race2` currently exist on disk).

**Target**: (-55, 115, -17), constant across all 18 goto attempts. Route class `MEDIUM_ASCENT`, profile `HAUL` throughout — the generous long-haul search profile, not a stingy one.

**Wedge point A** (2 firings, early in the episode): (-3, 96, 5).

**Wedge point B, the real prize** (8 of 10 firings, all `displaced:false`, every retry `stuck`/`path_timeout`): **(2, 101, 2)**.

**The one cell that worked**: (4, 100, 2) — the 10th `_reposition()` call, the only `displaced:true`. Just +2X/-1Y from wedge point B — well inside the existing 8-candidate offset range. Whatever traps (2,101,2) doesn't extend two blocks over.

Plan per team-lead: world-race2 gets archived once run #2 concludes (not deleted), then I take a dedicated test bot to these exact coords and diagnose whether this is (a) a genuine geometry trap (bowl rim / overhang / ledge), (b) a candidate-generation bug (offset list missing the real escape direction), or (c) a candidate-validation bug (a real standable cell exists but gets wrongly rejected). That answer decides whether `_reposition` needs smarter candidates or the observed 10% rate is geometry-fair.

Full writeup in FEEDBACK.md, commit 8e2b89c. Interim deployment note stands: "recovers wedges but slowly at hard geometry — 9min worst case observed."
**Wedge diagnosis, first pass**: world-race2 freed up after gear-race run #2 concluded. Spawned a dedicated test bot on it, called `S.recoveryDetect.findRepositionTarget` directly at the staked wedge point (2,101,2) — bypassing the walk entirely, pure read.

**It found a real candidate.** Offset `[2,0]` (the same offset the original bot's successful 10th attempt used) resolves to `{x:4.5, y:99, z:2.5}` — a genuine one-deep-dip standable cell. Dumped the full 8-offset scan; most others are either solid at the bot's own level or genuinely no floor within range (correctly skipped).

**This refutes "geometry defeats all 8 candidates."** The search is a pure, deterministic function of `(bx,by,bz,world)` — called from the identical cell with an unchanged world, it returns the identical answer every time. If the 9 failed attempts genuinely originated from this same cell (as their floored telemetry shows), the search would have found this same candidate on all 9 — meaning candidate generation/validation were very likely never the problem.

One honest gap: the candidate found here is `y:99`, but the historically recorded successful escape was `y:100` — one block higher. Can't fully resolve from floored-only pre-precision-fix telemetry whether this is sub-block drift or the walk just failing to complete a drop into the dip 9 times before succeeding on the 10th. Current lean: the WALK execution (`_reposition`'s 1.5s dead-reckoning forward+jump), not candidate generation, is the more likely culprit — pending direct confirmation via either instrumenting the walk loop or a controlled re-trigger.

Full writeup in FEEDBACK.md (54d54cc). Not fully closed — flagging the lean, not a verdict.
**Second diagnosis pass on the staked wild-wedge geometry (2,101,2), continuing 54d54cc.**

Confirmed the predecessor's finding with a clean positive control: replayed `_reposition`'s exact search+lookAt+walk logic from a fresh, grounded teleport to the exact wedge cell, 6/6 identical runs succeed in ~700ms. Candidate generation/validation is exonerated — the maneuver and geometry are both sound from a clean start.

**New finding: a real, previously-undocumented robustness gap.** `_reposition()` never clears any inherited movement control state (sneak, in particular) before issuing its own forward+jump. Deliberately holding `sneak` active going into the walk (a state it could inherit from whatever ran immediately before — the pathfinder library's own movement handling, or anything else upstream) reproduces the ORIGINAL incident's exact symptom deterministically: 3/3 runs, `candidateFound:true`, barely moves horizontally, never completes the required 2-block drop, stalls short of the arrival radius. Sneaking near a ledge in vanilla prevents walking off the edge at all — exactly the maneuver R2 needs here, and `_reposition` has no guard against it.

A second, adjacent gap: chaining `_reposition`'s walk with zero settle time immediately onto `_unstick`'s own 350ms jump+back hop (a genuine real neighbor in the code path) reliably leaves the bot airborne with residual velocity, producing a different failure shape (overshoot past the candidate, 5/5 runs) — same root cause class (no clean-state guarantee), different manifestation.

**Honest limitation**: I sampled `getControlState('sneak')` through a real, unmodified pathfinder crossing of this exact gap and it stayed false throughout a successful crossing — so I have not confirmed sneak (under the original incident's specific HAUL profile) is what actually fired live. Candidate generation is exonerated with a clean positive control; a real, reproducible `_reposition` bug is proven to exist and to produce the exact symptom when triggered; which inherited state (if any) is the historical live trigger for THIS wedge specifically remains open.

**Recommendation, actionable either way**: `_reposition()` should defensively clear sneak/sprint/directional control states and wait briefly (capped, e.g. 300-500ms) for `onGround` before walking — closes both demonstrated failure modes, converts the primitive from "trusts inherited state" to "always starts clean." Full writeup in FEEDBACK.md. Left world-race2 (25600/25601) and KrachKuddel (3161) running/parked for whoever picks up the `_reposition` fix.
## Fixed: `_reposition()` now clears inherited control state before walking (skills.js v58)

Picked up engine-dev's second-pass diagnosis (FEEDBACK.md, same date): `_reposition()` never
cleared any inherited movement control state before issuing its own forward+jump.

**Fix**: explicitly clear `sneak`/`sprint`/`back`/`left`/`right`, then wait briefly (capped
~400ms, never open-ended — `onGround` is separately known to stick false forever on some feet
blocks) for `onGround` before walking.

**Live verification**, on the exact geometry engine-dev diagnosed the bug on (KrachKuddel,
world-race2's staked R2 wedge): baseline, forced-sneak, and a simulated post-`_unstick`
airborne state, 5 runs each. All 15 land within the 1.2-block arrival radius of the found
candidate — genuinely reaching it, not merely `displaced:true` (the old overshoot failure was
also `displaced:true`, so that alone can't distinguish fixed from broken; checked real final
distance instead).

Also exposed `S.recoveryDetect.reposition()` so this never again needs a genuinely-staged
wedge to test — it calls the real `_reposition()` via `makeCtx`, not a hand-copied replay.
New permanent fixture: `bench/fixtures/reposition-cleanstate.sh` (self-contained geometry on
the local server, 8/8 clean after two fixture-construction bugs found and fixed along the
way — documented in its own header). Full preflight: 187/187.

**Fixed and verified live against a real mob, matching RotzRudi's exact death shape (survival.js v9, commit 5999820).**

`pick()` now verifies `fillerItem()` before choosing WALL_OFF at all when a real threat is present — no filler falls through to two new branches instead of a guaranteed no-op: `FIGHT_BACK` (reuses BREAK_LOS's own counter-attack gate, weapon held + threat already adjacent, deliberately without its health floor since the alternative here is guaranteed unopposed damage) or `FLEE_AWAY` (the absolute floor, generalizes `branchCreeper`'s own proven `GoalInvert(GoalFollow(...))` retreat to any threat, needs no inventory and no specific reachable target). Corner-step-for-melee was rejected per the design discussion — its value is breaking line of sight, which melee pathfinding doesn't need.

**No regression**: `survival-cannotheal.js` 7/7, full preflight 199/199, `flee-home-reachability.sh` still PASS.

**Live-mob proof, real zombie, not `drill()`**: staged the exact RotzRudi shape — melee threat adjacent, no filler, weapon held, HP crossing below 6. `FIGHT_BACK` fired and **killed the zombie** (confirmed via the `rotten_flesh` drop landing in inventory, not just the branch's own self-report) — the bot survived at 7 HP instead of dying. Separately verified `FLEE_AWAY` with zero equipment against a real zombie: genuine repeated distance gains (confirmed via real position deltas), survived 28+ seconds of active fleeing before eventually losing to a persistent attacker with literally nothing in hand — an honest limit, not a failure; #96's argument never claimed `FLEE_AWAY` guarantees survival with nothing at all, only that it replaces a guaranteed no-op with a genuine chance.

One adjacent, pre-existing noise pattern surfaced during this exact verification (not a regression from it): once a threat is defeated but HP hasn't recovered above the panic threshold yet, the no-filler `WALL_OFF` fallback re-triggers every ~200-250ms with repeated chat spam until natural regen catches up. Filed separately as #100 (not lethal, a noise/efficiency question distinct from this issue's own "zero defense" claim) with a likely fix pointer (generalize #92's own `g.standdown` mechanism).

Full writeup in FEEDBACK.md.
