## Agenda-side question, answered (read-only analysis, survival.js/pick() untouched)

Team-lead asked two specific questions after ruling survival.js off-limits to me for this
one. Answers from primary-source reading, not inference:

**(1) WHY does each panic entry cancel the running task — is there an agenda-side "cancel-on-
entry vs cancel-on-action" lever?** No — the premise doesn't hold. The cancellation is not
agenda.js's code at all: `survival.js`'s `enter()` calls `__skills.stop('panic')` (plus
`bot.pvp.forceStop()`, pathfinder goal clear, etc.) synchronously and unconditionally at the
very top of every entry — before `pick()` even runs to decide a branch, let alone what that
branch will do. `enter()` fires directly from a health-listener callback, entirely outside
agenda's own tick cycle. `agenda.js`'s REFLEX rung only reacts on its own ~2s tick, reading
`s.survivalActive` AFTER the task is already dead — its `act()` is `clearActiveTask()`,
confirmed pure bookkeeping (`A.activeTaskId = null` etc.), it never itself stops anything.
There's no point in the agenda ladder where this could be intercepted; any "defer the stop
until pick() knows what will happen" hardening has to live inside `enter()`/`pick()` itself.

**(2) Does #92 standdown's scope (branch-level vs entry-level) explain the miss?** Yes,
exactly, same shape as this issue's already-diagnosed root cause. Standdown's *gating* is
entry-level (checked at the top of every `enter()` call). Its *arming* is narrowly
branch-result-level — only `out.branch === 'WALL_OFF' && out.cannotHeal` sets it, not a
general "genuinely unrecoverable" signal independent of which branch handled it. The #99 fix
(populating `cannotHeal` on the no-filler bail) is a narrow instance of that broader scoping
choice — any future branch outcome that's also genuinely cannot-heal would need its own
explicit wiring, because the check is keyed to `WALL_OFF` specifically. Whether to broaden
arming to `threatsNow().length===0 && cannotHeal()` regardless of branch is a design call for
whoever owns this next — flagging, not building.

Full writeup in FEEDBACK.md. No edits made to survival.js or pick() during this pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
**Confirmed: the fix is already live, in commit 5999820 (#96's own commit) — no separate commit needed.**

engine-dev-3's fix landed on disk while I was mid-verification of #96 in the same uncommitted file, and got swept into my `git add survival.js` for #96 without either of us noticing at the time. Confirmed via `git diff` (zero uncommitted changes) and `grep` (the fixed return is in place). Independently verified the live specimen: SabberSepp's `GET /state` now shows `health:10.17, food:14`, agenda back to normal `RESTOCK/chopTrees` — the thrash is over.

**Regression question, answered from git history, not inference**: `git log -S"reason: 'no_filler'"` shows this early-return has existed since the original foundational commit, untouched since. `git show 71eb13f -- survival.js` (71eb13f = #92/v6, where `cannotHeal` was introduced) shows zero changes to this line. **This is a v6-era gap in #92's own original work — not a regression from #94 (v7), #98 (v8), or #96 (v9).** Each of those commits' own diffs confirms none of them touched `branchWallOff` at all. ## Finding 3 fixed: REFLEX no longer deadlocks forever on a threat that's visible but unreachable

By the time I looked at the live specimen, RotzRudi had already been moved off the isolated
platform by your manual `come` intervention (onto real ground, `onGround:true`) — so finding
1 (isolated platform, no legal path) is now historical rather than something I could still
verify live. What WAS still reproducing live, unprompted: `danger.state` pinned at "panic"
continuously (two zombies at d~3.2-3.4, `los:true`) while `survivalActive:false` the whole
time and health genuinely stable — exactly finding 3.

**Root cause**: dangerscan's panic score is LOS-based by design (no reachability check —
that's deliberate, it's meant to see through walls). REFLEX's old fire()/clear() read raw
`dangerState` alone, so it fired forever regardless of whether survival.js was doing anything,
and its own act() just yields — accomplishing nothing while blocking the entire ladder. That's
the exact mechanism behind the ~19 dead minutes.

**Fix** (conservative — REFLEX is safety:true): rather than touch dangerscan's scoring (risk
of ever missing a real threat), `sense()` now requires TWO corroborating signals before REFLEX
stands down on a still-panicking read: a sustained "panic + survival inactive" window
(20s) AND zero health lost during that entire window. Either breaking resets it. Verified
three ways: dry-run rung-wiring, live stateful tracking (goes stale at exactly 20s; a health
drop or survival engaging mid-streak correctly keeps it non-stale), and a live end-to-end
check through the real running tick() showing REFLEX held the full window then genuinely
released on its own. Full preflight 199/199.

Committed: e978d48 (fix), dc60dbc (FEEDBACK).

**Leaving this issue open** for findings 1, 2, and 4 — 1 needs real design work (what recovery
action even makes sense with zero inventory on an isolated platform) and I have no live case
to verify against anymore; 2 is the same shape as #95's two held follow-ups, treating this as
evidence toward that decision rather than building it unilaterally; 4 is outside the bot
engine's control (vanilla respawn placement).

## Bonus mystery (item 4) resolved: not a leak, WALL_OFF spent it as designed filler

Traced RotzRudi's own ledger minute-by-minute rather than guessing. Cobblestone genuinely
sat flat at 26 through 17:45:33Z-17:46:03Z. Then: a `panic phase:'enter' branch:'hp'` at
hp:7 → hp:4.5, followed by **three separate `death` events** (17:46:37Z, 17:46:54Z,
17:47:05Z — the bot kept respawning back into the same multi-zombie mess). The very first
`task_start` after the first death already shows `inv:{}` — vanilla drop-on-death, exactly
as expected.

The `kit_violation` you saw at ~17:46:34Z sits 3 seconds *before* that first death, while
still alive but critical — so the cobblestone was gone from a different, legitimate sink
first: `branchWallOff` places up to ~13 cobblestone per seal attempt, and the same window
shows many `panic phase:'recovered' branch:'WALL_OFF'` records firing in extremely tight
succession (six within one logged second). Consistent with ~2 wall-off attempts spending the
~24-26 held cobblestone before a third attempt found the kit genuinely empty. Not a leak —
filler is a designed consumable, consumed as designed, repeatedly, until exhausted.

**What IS worth flagging**: those aren't one wall-off completing normally — they're rapid
enter/recovered pairs (danger re-triggers immediately after each declared recovery), each
apparently bailing early at critical HP. Three deaths in under 30 seconds despite WALL_OFF
being the designated defense the whole time — a defense cycling too fast to actually defend,
not an accounting bug. Routing this to engine-dev's survival.js lane directly since they're
already mid-iteration on exactly this area (#94/#98) with much fresher context than I have.

Full trace in FEEDBACK.md (2026-09-02, "#97 bonus mystery resolved").

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
## Items 2 and 3, argued and (partially) built

**Item 3 (decider re-dispatch gap) — built.** `decider.js` now tracks `(position, why,
lastError)` at every genuinely-new-episode attempt. If a new episode matches the immediately
prior one on all three (bot hasn't moved, same stall reason, same underlying error), the
whole decision is skipped — no rules lookup, no Andy call — and the episode is closed via the
same `dirClose` #95 built (`closedBy:'frozen_repeat'`) instead of blindly re-dispatching the
identical failing call. Deliberately the narrow fix, reusing existing verified machinery
rather than building #95's two held follow-ups (a more specific `why`, RESTOCK's repeat-count
feeding direction) — your field evidence here is real, but unholding those is still
team-lead's call once soak #3's numbers land.

Verified in isolation (6 cases: first attempt never flags, a repeat is caught on the 2nd AND
3rd occurrence, real movement clears it, same position + different why/lastError doesn't
false-positive, two bots never cross-contaminate). Deliberately **not** exercised against the
live decider process yet — soak #3 is running on that shared daemon right now, and I don't
want to restart it mid-measurement. Will do the live end-to-end check at the next safe
restart (soak #3's window close).

**Item 2 (generalize stuck/ESCAPE beyond underground) — argued, not built.** Two reasons: no
live specimen exists anymore to verify against (you'd already gotten RotzRudi back onto real
ground before I started diagnosis), and the missing piece is genuinely a new, safety-critical
skill, not just a detection tweak — `ascendToSurface` is the wrong direction for a
surface-stranded bot, and the existing candidate search (`findRepositionTarget`) only scans 5
blocks down, nowhere near enough to have found your actual 5-6 block drop. A wrong
fall-damage/landing calculation is the kind of bug that kills the bot it's meant to save.
Proposing a new `emergencyDescend`-class skill (survivable-fall search + execute) triggered by
a detection arm matching your own suggested shape (N consecutive zero-progress attempts,
`surfaceExposed` gate removed) — but staging a fresh fixture first rather than shipping this
from reasoning alone. Full argument in FEEDBACK.md.

Item 4 (cobblestone mystery) is closed — see my earlier comment and engine-dev's much deeper
follow-up confirming the exact mechanism and why #94's fix doesn't cover the melee case.

2089	what: team-lead's wait-filler assignment while soak #2's window ran. Swept every `jget` call site across all 18 `bench/fixtures/*.sh` files (97 sites total) for the false->"null" misread bug (#93, jget() fixed by engine-dev-3).
2090	
2091	METHOD: the bug only matters where the underlying JSON value is a real boolean that could legitimately be `false` (never affects strings/numbers, and never affects `true` — jq's `//` only misfires on `false`/`null`/missing alike). Grepped every site comparing a jget'd value against `"true"`/`"false"`, then traced each to its source. Key structural finding: the dominant pattern in this codebase is `[[ "$(jget ...)" == "true" ]] || fail ...` (or the `!=` mirror) — a POSITIVE gate that treats "anything other than true" as failure. That pattern is **immune** to the bug: a real `false` and a misread `"null"` both fail the `==true` test identically, so the branch fires the same way either way. Only a NEGATIVE gate that explicitly distinguishes `"false"` from other non-true values (`== "false"` or `!= "false"`) is actually at risk.
2092	
2093	RESULTS:
2094	- **97/97 sites checked.**
2095	- **3 sites where a real boolean `false` could have been misread as `"null"` with a behavioral consequence**, all already known or now closed:
2096	  1. `dangerscan-canopy.sh:109` (`stoneOpen == "false"`) — the bug's OWN discovery site. Already fixed and live-reverified (engine-dev-3, both directions: leaf canopy correctly reads open, real stone ceiling still correctly reads enclosed).
2097	  2. `craft-void.sh:35` (`$ok != "false"`) — could have let a genuine `craftSafe` `ok:false` pass unfailed. Already spot-checked by the issue's own author post-fix: still passes cleanly, no live bug was hiding behind it (craftSafe returns `ok:true` in current practice).
2098	  3. `induced-stress-sequencing.sh:115` (`skelAliveVal == "false"`) — the flagged priority site, survival.js QA lane. Traced precisely: pre-fix, a genuinely-dead skeleton read as `"null"` instead of `"false"`, so the fast-exit branch (`stableChecks>=2`) could never fire via a real kill. **Critically, this does NOT corrupt the fixture's pass/fail verdict** — all three real checks (breakLosSeen fired, no thrash, hpMin>=6) run unconditionally after the loop regardless of why it ended, and are cumulative/monotonic over the whole observed window (hpMin is a running minimum, thrash-detection scans the full RUNG_SEQ, breakLosSeen is a sticky flag). A longer-than-intended observation window can only make a PASS verdict MORE trustworthy, never less — the bug's only real cost was wasted wall-clock time (always running the full `SEQ_TIMEOUT` instead of exiting ~4s after genuine stabilization).
2099	- **Every other site is the immune `==true`/`!=true` pattern**, or (payload-persist.sh:43/46) compares a version NUMBER against `"false"` — a branch that's practically unreachable regardless of the bug, since a payload version is never legitimately `0`/`false`.
2100	
2101	**ANSWER to team-lead's specific question — fixtures whose historical green was false: ZERO.** No fixture in this sweep ever reported a false PASS because of this bug. The bug's failure direction was consistently "a real problem might silently not get flagged as clearly/quickly as intended," never "a real problem got hidden behind a false PASS."   1. `dangerscan-canopy.sh:109` (`stoneOpen == "false"`) — the bug's OWN discovery site. Already fixed and live-reverified (engine-dev-3, both directions: leaf canopy correctly reads open, real stone ceiling still correctly reads enclosed).
  2. `craft-void.sh:35` (`$ok != "false"`) — could have let a genuine `craftSafe` `ok:false` pass unfailed. Already spot-checked by the issue's own author post-fix: still passes cleanly, no live bug was hiding behind it (craftSafe returns `ok:true` in current practice).
  3. `induced-stress-sequencing.sh:115` (`skelAliveVal == "false"`) — the flagged priority site, survival.js QA lane. Traced precisely: pre-fix, a genuinely-dead skeleton read as `"null"` instead of `"false"`, so the fast-exit branch (`stableChecks>=2`) could never fire via a real kill. **Critically, this does NOT corrupt the fixture's pass/fail verdict** — all three real checks (breakLosSeen fired, no thrash, hpMin>=6) run unconditionally after the loop regardless of why it ended, and are cumulative/monotonic over the whole observed window (hpMin is a running minimum, thrash-detection scans the full RUNG_SEQ, breakLosSeen is a sticky flag). A longer-than-intended observation window can only make a PASS verdict MORE trustworthy, never less — the bug's only real cost was wasted wall-clock time (always running the full `SEQ_TIMEOUT` instead of exiting ~4s after genuine stabilization).
- **Every other site is the immune `==true`/`!=true` pattern**, or (payload-persist.sh:43/46) compares a version NUMBER against `"false"` — a branch that's practically unreachable regardless of the bug, since a payload version is never legitimately `0`/`false`.

**ANSWER to team-lead's specific question — fixtures whose historical green was false: ZERO.** No fixture in this sweep ever reported a false PASS because of this bug. The bug's failure direction was consistently "a real problem might silently not get flagged as clearly/quickly as intended," never "a real problem got hidden behind a false PASS." (`dangerscan-canopy.sh` is the interesting inverse case: the bug caused false REDS on genuinely-correct code, not false greens.)

**LIVE RE-VERIFICATION of the priority site, as asked** (fresh agenda-enabled QA bot ZoffZenzi/3172, isolated on 25600 far from both the soak and #54's wedge area, per the shared-server discipline): ran `induced-stress-sequencing.sh` twice against survival v6. **Neither run's fast-exit actually fired** — both took the full ~93s wall-clock (setup+90s timeout+teardown), same as before the jget fix. This is NOT a residual jget bug (confirmed by reading: `skelAliveVal` now correctly reads `"false"` post-fix) — it's that the fast-exit's OWN precondition (skeleton confirmed dead, HP stable) genuinely never became true within the window in either run, because the skeleton stayed alive and effective the whole time.

**SEPARATE, more urgent finding surfaced by this**, outside #93's own scope but worth flagging loudly: **both live runs saw the bot reach severe near-death** — 0.33 HP and 0.17 HP respectively, worse than this fixture's own previously-recorded worst case (1.83 HP, cited in its own header comment as the reason the hpMin<6 check exists at all). Rung sequences (`REFLEX IDLE REFLEX IDLE POSTURE REFLEX IDLE REFLEX IDLE`) show REFLEX repeatedly firing and clearing while a single skeleton stayed engaged — consistent with BREAK_LOS's OWN documented pre-existing weakness (this file's #65 header notes: "BREAK_LOS can end a run reporting 'recovered' while the threat is still adjacent"), not anything touched by #92's fix (which only changed WALL_OFF and the orchestration standdown gate, never BREAK_LOS itself). Both fixture runs correctly FAILED on the hpMin<6 criterion — the fixture's own doctrine ("a near-death is not a pass on its own") worked exactly as designed and caught a real, sharp near-death both times. Flagging rather than root-causing further (out of scope for this audit and the soak-grading clock): worth a dedicated follow-up on whether BREAK_LOS's repeated-engagement handling has gotten WORSE, or these two runs were just unlucky RNG against a single aggressive skeleton — 2 data points is not enough to tell.
